documented_diagnosis.name: Basal cell carcinoma
documented_diagnosis.evidence: Confirmed by biopsy, as recorded in PAD-UFES-20.

teaching_points: A shiny, pink, pearl-like bump is a classic look of nodular basal cell carcinoma, the most common skin cancer.
It grows slowly and rarely spreads, but untreated it can damage the surrounding skin.
Most appear on sun-exposed skin of the head, neck, upper trunk and limbs.

look_alikes.name: Intradermal nevus
look_alikes.note: Soft, skin-coloured or light brown, usually present and unchanged for years.

look_alikes.name: Amelanotic melanoma
look_alikes.note: Pink and featureless but often growing quickly; needs urgent assessment.

look_alikes.name: Squamous cell carcinoma
look_alikes.note: Firmer and scalier, often with a crusted surface.
